smell: install.sh declares and expands a bash array (`_gh_auth_header=()` / `${_gh_auth_header[@]}`) but the README and install.sh's own usage docstring direct users to pipe the script into `sh`. On Debian/Ubuntu where `/bin/sh` is `dash`, the script syntax-errors at the array declaration before any download starts, leaving the user with a cryptic `Syntax error: "(" unexpected` instead of an installed binary. The shebang `#!/usr/bin/env bash` is ignored when the script is read via stdin by `sh`.
evidence:
# README / docstring: curl -sSfL .../install.sh | sh
_gh_auth_header=()
if [ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    _gh_auth_header=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN")
fi
VERSION=$(curl ... "${_gh_auth_header[@]}" ...)
severity_reason: rubric §4/known-exploit-path-equivalent — install.sh is the documented entry point and silently fails on the dominant Linux distros (Debian/Ubuntu/derivatives) where /bin/sh is dash; users hit a cryptic syntax error during the published one-liner install and may retry blind or fall back to unverified manual binary fetches.
fix_summary: Either (a) replace the README invocation with `| bash` (and update the install.sh docstring on line 10), matching helm.sh and k3s.io patterns; or (b) make the auth header POSIX-compatible by inlining the conditional: `if [ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then VERSION=$(curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" ...); else VERSION=$(curl ...); fi`. Option (a) is one character per doc site and matches the shebang's intent.
rule_source: CWE-94 (silent script failure)
ShellCheck SC3030 (in POSIX sh, arrays are undefined)
repo-counter-example: scripts/install.sh:1 (#!/usr/bin/env bash declares bash, README pipes to sh)
must_preserve: the GITHUB_TOKEN rate-limit-lift behavior; cosign + sha256 verification chain

smell: `INSECURE=1` is an env-var fail-open switch that disables SHA256 verification across the entire install. When cosign is not present (the common case on a clean dev box), setting INSECURE=1 disables BOTH the cosign signature check AND the sha256 check, leaving zero integrity guards. The warning printed is loud but the install still proceeds; an attacker who can prepend env vars to a piped invocation (`INSECURE=1 curl … | sh` in pasted instructions) bypasses every guard.
evidence:
INSECURE="${INSECURE:-}"
if [ -n "$INSECURE" ]; then
    if [ -n "$COSIGN_CMD" ]; then
        printf 'WARNING: INSECURE=1 ... SHA256 SKIPPED (cosign still active).\n' >&2
    else
        printf 'WARNING: INSECURE=1 ... SHA256 and cosign SKIPPED.\n' >&2
    fi
severity_reason: rubric §4/credential-exposure-equivalent — the integrity bypass is one-shell-var away from a successful supply-chain substitution; the docstring presents sha256sum-missing as a valid reason to flip the switch when in fact installing coreutils is the right answer.
fix_summary: Either (a) require `INSECURE=1` AND a separate `I_UNDERSTAND_THE_RISK=yes` to bypass; (b) when sha256sum is missing, refuse and tell the user to install coreutils rather than offering an env-var skip; or (c) when cosign is absent AND INSECURE is set, fail-closed and require `--no-cosign --no-sha256` on a wrapper rather than a single env var. Option (b) is smallest change with largest gain — sha256sum ships with coreutils on every Linux distro install.sh supports.
rule_source: CWE-494 (download of code without integrity check)
CWE-345 (insufficient verification of data authenticity)
CLAUDE.md §security-invariants — never weaken integrity gates
must_preserve: the cosign verification path when cosign is installed (it is independent of INSECURE today and that's correct)

smell: The `curl_safe` wrapper centralizes hardened curl flags (HTTPS-only, TLS 1.2 floor, connect/transfer timeouts, retry policy), but the latest-release resolution call does not use it — it inlines a partial subset of those flags. The retry-on-connrefused behavior the wrapper provides is silently absent at exactly the call site most likely to fail (GitHub API rate-limit / transient 5xx).
fix_summary: Replace the inline curl with `curl_safe -sSfL --max-time 30 "${_gh_auth_header[@]}" "..."`. The wrapper's `--max-time 120` is overridden by the second `--max-time 30` (curl uses last value). Net change: ~3 lines.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: scripts/install.sh:38 (curl_safe defined for exactly this purpose)
Go proverb: a little copying is better than a little dependency — but only when copies stay in sync

smell: The lint-shell job restricts shellcheck's `scandir` to `./scripts` only, so `.github/scripts/coverage-check.sh` (an 82-line bash script with associative arrays, process substitution, and bc-based arithmetic running in CI) is never linted. Any shellcheck-class regression in coverage-check.sh — quoting bug, unguarded var expansion, broken associative-array key — slips past CI and only manifests as a confusing CI failure when the floor logic mis-triggers.
evidence:
lint-shell:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@...
      - uses: ludeeus/action-shellcheck@... # 2.0.0
        with:
          severity: warning
          scandir: "./scripts"
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — coverage-check.sh gates the test-go job, so a silent break here either fails CI cryptically or, worse, lets a coverage regression slip if a quoting bug zeroes a parsed value.
fix_summary: Drop the `scandir: "./scripts"` line so action-shellcheck scans the whole tree (its default), or set `scandir: "."` explicitly. Optionally add `additional_files: ".github/scripts"` if you want to keep `./scripts` as the primary path. Net effect: one less line of config; coverage-check.sh becomes lint-protected.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §tooling — `lint-yaml`, `validate-terraform` etc. all in CI; lint-shell should match scope
ShellCheck wiki — recommended for any non-trivial shell script
must_preserve: the action-shellcheck SHA pin and version trailer

smell: The tar extraction uses `--no-same-owner --no-same-permissions` for hardening but does not pass `--no-overwrite-dir` or pre-validate the archive contents (`tar -tzf` listing) before extracting. A malicious archive could in theory contain `..`-prefixed entries or symlinks that escape `$TMP`. The cosign + sha256 chain is the primary guard so this is genuine defense-in-depth, but GNU tar's default behavior on `..` entries varies by version and a one-line listing-validation costs nothing.
evidence:
info "extracting"
cd "$TMP"
tar --no-same-owner --no-same-permissions -xzf "$ARCHIVE_NAME"

[ -f "$BINARY" ] || die "$BINARY not found in archive"
fix_summary: Add `--no-overwrite-dir` and consider pre-listing: `tar -tzf "$ARCHIVE_NAME" | grep -qE '^(\.\.|/)' && die 'archive contains absolute or parent-traversal paths'`. Goreleaser tarballs are flat and clean today, but a single line cheaply enforces it.
rule_source: CWE-22 (path traversal)
Tarbomb (Wikipedia) — historic risk pattern from `tar` archives with absolute or `..` paths
must_preserve: the cosign + sha256 verification ordering (must run BEFORE extract)

smell: `environments/production/variables.tf` ships hardcoded defaults that look operator-specific: `target_node = "pve01"`, `cluster_name = "grappleberry"`, `vmid_base = 7000`. terraform.tfvars is gitignored, but anyone running `terraform apply` without overrides would deploy with these defaults silently. The `production` directory name implies this is the canonical example for prod deploys; defaults should be intentionally absent for variables with no sensible cross-environment value, so terraform errors with `target_node is required`.
fix_summary: For variables with no sensible cross-environment default (target_node, cluster_name, vmid_base), drop the `default` attribute so terraform fails fast with a missing-required error. Keep defaults on infrastructure shape vars (cpu_cores, memory_mb). Net change: ~5 deletions in variables.tf.
rule_source: HashiCorp Terraform docs — Input Variables: "If no default is set, the variable is required"
tflint terraform_required_version + terraform_required_providers preset (already enabled at .tflint.hcl:9)
must_preserve: the variable types and validation behavior in the module

smell: The production environment's variables redeclare every module variable but drop the `validation` blocks present on the module (cpu_cores 2-32, memory_mb >= 8192, master_count odd 1-5, vmid_base 100-9000, etc.). The module's validation will fire eventually but only AFTER terraform plan resolves the module reference, producing later/less-pinpointed errors. The duplicated-but-loosened variables here are a missed early-validation opportunity and create two specs that can drift.
fix_summary: Either (a) delete the duplicated env-level vars and let the module own validation (the env's main.tf passes them straight through anyway); or (b) mirror the module's validation blocks here for fail-fast errors. Option (a) is the smaller diff and aligns with module-as-source-of-truth.
rule_source: HashiCorp Terraform docs — Input Variables (validation precondition vs module precondition)
DRY principle
must_preserve: the env's variable surface that callers (operators / CI) depend on by name

smell: The HCL header documents `PROXMOX_VE_INSECURE` as "set to 'true' to disable tls verification" without a security warning. The bpg/proxmox provider supports this env var; documenting it without flagging it as a development-only knob normalizes TLS-disable as a routine operator action. Same comment is duplicated in `variables.tf` and the production environment's variables.tf.
evidence:
# uses environment variables:
# - PROXMOX_VE_ENDPOINT    (api url, e.g., https://pve.example.com:8006/)
# - PROXMOX_VE_USERNAME    (username, e.g., root@pam)
# - PROXMOX_VE_PASSWORD    (password)
# - PROXMOX_VE_INSECURE    (optional, set to "true" to disable tls verification)
fix_summary: Append a one-line warning to the comment in all three sites: `# - PROXMOX_VE_INSECURE  (DEV ONLY: disables TLS verification — never set in prod; use a CA-signed cert or add the proxmox CA to your trust store)`.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §security-invariants — never recommend InsecureSkipVerify
CWE-295 (improper certificate validation)
must_preserve: the env-var contract with bpg/proxmox provider

smell: The script's `Requires:` docstring lists `bash, curl, tar, sha256sum` — but does not mention that the script ALSO requires bash specifically (not sh) when invoked via `curl | sh`. Combined with the array-syntax issue (separate finding), users on Debian/Ubuntu reading only the README never learn the dependency until the script crashes.
evidence: # Requires: bash, curl, tar, sha256sum. Optionally: cosign (highly recommended).
fix_summary: If the bash-array fix is option (a) `| bash`, this finding resolves automatically when the README and docstring update. If option (b) (POSIX-compatible auth), this finding becomes moot. Either way, no separate fix needed once `iac:e076e43c:sh-bash-array-dash-incompat` is addressed.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: scripts/install.sh:10 (docstring uses `| sh`)
Go proverb: documentation is for human readers
must_preserve: the Requires line itself once corrected
